review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

24:1.sourceText: τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ὄρθρου βαθέως ἐπὶ τὸ μνῆμα ἦλθον φέρουσαι ἃ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα.
24:1.targetText: On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared.

groups.note: The feminine μιᾷ ("one") implies ἡμέρᾳ and is rendered as the ordinal first; the dative of time supplies On.
βαθέως ("deep") with ὄρθρου ("dawn") is rendered very early.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The relative ἅ ("which") is left implicit in the English the spices they had prepared.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending and the feminine participle.
English supplies the noun day that the feminine μιᾷ implies; N1904 has no word for it.

24:2.sourceText: εὗρον δὲ τὸν λίθον ἀποκεκυλισμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου,
24:2.targetText: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb,

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

24:3.sourceText: εἰσελθοῦσαι δὲ οὐχ εὗρον τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.
24:3.targetText: but when they entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.

24:4.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἀπορεῖσθαι αὐτὰς περὶ τούτου καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο ἐπέστησαν αὐταῖς ἐν ἐσθῆτι ἀστραπτούσῃ·
24:4.targetText: While they were puzzling over this, suddenly two men in radiant apparel stood beside them.

groups.note: ἐν τῷ with the infinitive means "while".
ἰδού ("look") is rendered as suddenly.
ἀστραπτούσῃ means "flashing like lightning".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative frame καὶ ἐγένετο ("and it came about") untranslated.
BSB leaves untranslated the καί that brings in the main clause after ἐγένετο.

24:5.sourceText: ἐμφόβων δὲ γενομένων αὐτῶν καὶ κλινουσῶν τὰ πρόσωπα εἰς τὴν γῆν, εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτάς Τί ζητεῖτε τὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τῶν νεκρῶν;
24:5.targetText: As the women bowed their faces to the ground in terror, the two men asked them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?

groups.note: ἐμφόβων γενομένων ("becoming terrified") is rendered in terror.
BSB renders the pronoun αὐτῶν ("they") as the women.
The genitive absolute is rendered as an As-clause.
The article with the participle ("the one who lives") is rendered the living.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB merges the two participles into one As-clause, so this καί has no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speakers; the Greek has only the verb ending of εἶπαν.

24:6.sourceText: οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἀλλὰ ἠγέρθη. μνήσθητε ὡς ἐλάλησεν ὑμῖν ἔτι ὢν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ,
24:6.targetText: He is not here; He has risen! Remember how He told you while He was still in Galilee:

unmappedSource.reason: BSB joins the clauses with a semicolon, so ἀλλά ("but") has no separate English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

24:7.sourceText: λέγων τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὅτι δεῖ παραδοθῆναι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ σταυρωθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἀναστῆναι.
24:7.targetText: ‘The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.’”

groups.note: The dative of time ἡμέρᾳ supplies on.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves λέγων ("saying") unexpressed; the colon after told introduces the words.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The ὅτι after the fronted subject ("that he must") is not expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

24:9.sourceText: καὶ ὑποστρέψασαι ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπήγγειλαν ταῦτα πάντα τοῖς ἕνδεκα καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς λοιποῖς.
24:9.targetText: And when they returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to the Eleven and to all the others.

groups.note: The dative article τοῖς marks ἕνδεκα ("eleven"), a number that does not decline.

24:10.sourceText: ἦσαν δὲ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ Μαρία καὶ Ἰωάνα καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου· καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ σὺν αὐταῖς ἔλεγον πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ταῦτα.
24:10.targetText: It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told this to the apostles.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The article ἡ with the genitive Ἰακώβου ("the one of James") is rendered the mother of James.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
English lists the names with commas, so these καί have no separate English word.

24:11.sourceText: καὶ ἐφάνησαν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λῆρος τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα, καὶ ἠπίστουν αὐταῖς.
24:11.targetText: But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.

groups.note: This καί is contrastive; BSB renders it But.
The demonstrative ταῦτα ("these") is rendered their, pointing to the women's words.
ἠπίστουν means "they disbelieved".
BSB renders the pronoun αὐταῖς ("them") as the women.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

24:12.sourceText: [[Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἀναστὰς ἔδραμεν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον· καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει τὰ ὀθόνια μόνα· καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς αὑτὸν θαυμάζων τὸ γεγονός.]]
24:12.targetText: Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb. And after bending down and seeing only the linen cloths, he went away, wondering to himself what had happened.

groups.note: The present βλέπει ("he sees") is folded into the after-clause as seeing.
The article with the participle ("the thing that had happened") is rendered what had happened.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB folds the seeing into the after-clause, so this καί before went away has no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἀναστάς, rendered got up, to the main verb ran.
English joins bending down to seeing inside the after-clause; the Greek has the participle παρακύψας and the verb βλέπει without a conjunction.

24:13.sourceText: Καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἦσαν πορευόμενοι εἰς κώμην ἀπέχουσαν σταδίους ἑξήκοντα ἀπὸ Ἱερουσαλήμ, ᾗ ὄνομα Ἐμμαοῦς,
24:13.targetText: That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.

groups.note: ἀπέχουσαν σταδίους ἑξήκοντα ("sixty stadia distant") is converted to about seven miles.
ᾗ ὄνομα ("whose name was") is rendered called.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves Καὶ ἰδού ("and look") untranslated.
BSB's time phrase That same day needs no word for ἐν ("on").

24:14.sourceText: καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡμίλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους περὶ πάντων τῶν συμβεβηκότων τούτων.
24:14.targetText: They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.

groups.note: The article with the participle ("the things that had happened") is rendered that had happened.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
BSB leaves τούτων ("these") unexpressed after everything.

24:15.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὁμιλεῖν αὐτοὺς καὶ συνζητεῖν, καὶ αὐτὸς Ἰησοῦς ἐγγίσας συνεπορεύετο αὐτοῖς·
24:15.targetText: And as they talked and deliberated, Jesus Himself came up and walked along with them.

groups.note: ἐν τῷ with the infinitive means "as".
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula ἐγένετο ("it came about") untranslated.
BSB leaves untranslated the καί that brings in the main clause after ἐγένετο.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐγγίσας, rendered came up, to the main verb.

24:16.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν ἐκρατοῦντο τοῦ μὴ ἐπιγνῶναι αὐτόν.
24:16.targetText: But their eyes were kept from recognizing Him.

groups.note: τοῦ μή with the infinitive after a verb of restraining ("so as not to") is rendered from.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

24:17.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς Τίνες οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι οὓς ἀντιβάλλετε πρὸς ἀλλήλους περιπατοῦντες; καὶ ἐστάθησαν σκυθρωποί.
24:17.targetText: He asked them, “What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?”  They stood still, with sadness on their faces.

groups.note: ἀντιβάλλετε πρὸς ἀλλήλους ("you exchange with one another") is rendered discussing so intently.
σκυθρωποί means "looking sad".

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB recasts "What are these words that you exchange" as What are you discussing, so οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι οὕς ("these words that") has no separate English words.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.

24:18.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἷς ὀνόματι Κλεοπᾶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Σὺ μόνος παροικεῖς Ἱερουσαλὴμ καὶ οὐκ ἔγνως τὰ γενόμενα ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις;
24:18.targetText: One of them, named Cleopas, asked Him, “Are You the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in recent days?”

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς … εἶπεν ("answering … said") is rendered by the one verb asked.
παροικεῖς ("you are staying as a stranger") is rendered Are … visitor.
The subject of ἔγνως ("you knew") is rendered with the relative who.
The article with the participle ("the things that happened") is rendered the things that have happened.
ἐν αὐτῇ ("in it") is rendered there.
The demonstrative ταύταις ("these") is rendered recent.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB turns the second clause into a relative who-clause, so καί ("and") has no separate English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a partitive referring to the two travelers of 24:13.

24:19.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ποῖα; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Τὰ περὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζαρηνοῦ, ὃς ἐγένετο ἀνὴρ προφήτης δυνατὸς ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ ἐναντίον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ,
24:19.targetText: “What things?” He asked.  “The events involving Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered. “This man was a prophet, powerful in speech and action before God and all the people.

groups.note: The article οἱ with δέ works as the subject pronoun.
τοῦ Ναζαρηνοῦ ("the Nazarene") is rendered of Nazareth.
BSB starts a new sentence, rendering the relative ὅς ("who") as This.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") implicit after asked.
The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") implicit after answered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

24:20.sourceText: ὅπως τε παρέδωκαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ἡμῶν εἰς κρίμα θανάτου καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν.
24:20.targetText: Our chief priests and rulers delivered Him up to the sentence of death, and they crucified Him.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence, so ὅπως τε ("and how") has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

24:21.sourceText: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἠλπίζομεν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ μέλλων λυτροῦσθαι τὸν Ἰσραήλ· ἀλλά γε καὶ σὺν πᾶσιν τούτοις τρίτην ταύτην ἡμέραν ἄγει ἀφ’ οὗ ταῦτα ἐγένετο.
24:21.targetText: But we were hoping He was the One who would redeem Israel. And besides all this, it is the third day since these things took place.

groups.note: The article with the participle μέλλων ("the one about to") is rendered the One who would.
ἀλλά γε καί ("yes, and moreover") is rendered And.
The demonstrative ταύτην ("this") is rendered the.
The impersonal ἄγει ("it is passing") is rendered it is.
ἀφ’ οὗ ("from which time") is rendered since.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ὅτι ("that") unexpressed after were hoping.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

24:22.sourceText: ἀλλὰ καὶ γυναῖκές τινες ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξέστησαν ἡμᾶς, γενόμεναι ὀρθριναὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον,
24:22.targetText: Furthermore, some of our women astounded us. They were at the tomb early this morning,

groups.note: ἀλλὰ καί ("but also") is rendered Furthermore.
The participle γενόμεναι ("having been") is rendered as a new sentence, They were.

24:23.sourceText: καὶ μὴ εὑροῦσαι τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἦλθον λέγουσαι καὶ ὀπτασίαν ἀγγέλων ἑωρακέναι, οἳ λέγουσιν αὐτὸν ζῆν.
24:23.targetText: but they did not find His body. They came and told us they had seen a vision of angels, who said that Jesus was alive.

groups.note: This καί is contrastive; BSB renders it but.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("him").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle λέγουσαι, rendered told, to the main verb came.
English supplies the hearers of told; the Greek participle has no object.

24:24.sourceText: καὶ ἀπῆλθόν τινες τῶν σὺν ἡμῖν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ εὗρον οὕτως καθὼς καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες εἶπον, αὐτὸν δὲ οὐκ εἶδον.
24:24.targetText: Then some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had described. But Him they did not see.”

groups.note: τῶν σὺν ἡμῖν ("of those with us") is rendered of our companions.
οὕτως ("so, in this way") is rendered just, with as for καθώς.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

24:25.sourceText: καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ὦ ἀνόητοι καὶ βραδεῖς τῇ καρδίᾳ τοῦ πιστεύειν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐλάλησαν οἱ προφῆται·
24:25.targetText: Then Jesus said to them, “O foolish ones, how slow are your hearts to believe all that the prophets have spoken!

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτός ("he").
The article τῇ is rendered your.
The dative καρδίᾳ ("in heart") is recast as the subject your hearts.
The articular infinitive τοῦ πιστεύειν is rendered to believe.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB turns "and slow of heart" into the exclamation how slow are your hearts, so καί has no separate English word.
BSB renders πιστεύειν ἐπί ("believe in") with a direct object, so ἐπί has no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English turns the description into an exclamation.
English supplies the copula in the exclamation.

24:26.sourceText: οὐχὶ ταῦτα ἔδει παθεῖν τὸν Χριστὸν καὶ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ;
24:26.targetText: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then to enter His glory?”

groups.note: εἰσελθεῖν εἰς ("to go into") is rendered to enter.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

24:27.sourceText: καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ Μωϋσέως καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν προφητῶν διερμήνευσεν αὐτοῖς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς γραφαῖς τὰ περὶ ἑαυτοῦ.
24:27.targetText: And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.

groups.note: BSB's one with covers both ἀπό ("from") phrases.
The article τά ("the things") is rendered what.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies was written; the Greek has only τά ("the things") about Himself.

24:28.sourceText: Καὶ ἤγγισαν εἰς τὴν κώμην οὗ ἐπορεύοντο, καὶ αὐτὸς προσεποιήσατο πορρώτερον πορεύεσθαι.
24:28.targetText: As they approached the village where they were headed, He seemed to be going farther.

groups.note: ἤγγισαν εἰς ("drew near to") is rendered approached.
BSB makes the first of the two καί-joined clauses an As-clause, so the καί between them is rendered As.
προσεποιήσατο means "acted as though".

24:29.sourceText: καὶ παρεβιάσαντο αὐτὸν λέγοντες Μεῖνον μεθ’ ἡμῶν, ὅτι πρὸς ἑσπέραν ἐστὶν καὶ κέκλικεν ἤδη ἡ ἡμέρα. καὶ εἰσῆλθεν τοῦ μεῖναι σὺν αὐτοῖς.
24:29.targetText: But they pleaded with Him, “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening and the day is almost over.”  So He went in to stay with them.

groups.note: This καί is contrastive; BSB renders it But.
πρός ("toward") evening is rendered nearly evening.
κέκλικεν ("has declined") is rendered is almost over.
The articular infinitive τοῦ μεῖναι expresses purpose.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB introduces the plea as direct speech without λέγοντες ("saying").
BSB leaves ἤδη ("already") unexpressed; is almost over renders κέκλικεν.

24:30.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ κατακλιθῆναι αὐτὸν μετ’ αὐτῶν λαβὼν τὸν ἄρτον εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἐπεδίδου αὐτοῖς·

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative frame καὶ ἐγένετο ("and it came about") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

English joins the participle κλάσας, rendered broke, to the main verb gave.

24:31.sourceText: αὐτῶν δὲ διηνοίχθησαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ, καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτόν· καὶ αὐτὸς ἄφαντος ἐγένετο ἀπ’ αὐτῶν.
